doc.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26

title: Ory promotes his own dances and Pete Lala has the police stop them
summary: Ory leaves Pete Lala's to promote dances, Pete wants a cut, and sends cops to chase off his customers.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, that's what he was playing with me. I left there and I started promoting dance at the economy hall and the co-op radio hall. Pete got mad because I didn't cut him in on my dance. He sent about 50 cops around there and they ran all my customers away.
I packed up and left. I came to Los Angeles. That's what happened to Jelly right here in this town.
San Francisco. What? The cops running customers away. Yeah.
Just walk in and cement them. Yeah.
They just went out of the raid and that's that. That's what they went. Yeah. I was doing real fine too. Yeah. Because I was going to cut them in, you know.
Yeah. This place was too small. They couldn't hold enough people that I could make over nice work, you know.
For you in business you should make more than a salary, you know. Yeah.
You're promoting it. You're promoting it. You're going to hold all the expense and trouble. So then he wanted to cut in on me. I told him, no.
No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. He had the power, so you just don't go on down there and just write.
